title: Aytek Namitok — The “Voluntary” Adherence of Kabarda (Eastern Circassia) to Russia
lang: EN · TR · КАБ · РУС · DE · عر · АДЫ
description: Caucasian Review, Munich, 1956. A critique of the Soviet claim that Kabarda voluntarily joined Russia in 1557.

tr.title: Aytek Namitok — Kabarda’nın (Doğu Çerkesya’nın) Rusya’ya “Gönüllü” Katılımı
tr.description: Caucasian Review, Münih, Sayı 2, 1956, s. 17 vd. Aytek Namitok, 1956 tarihli bu makalesinde Kabardey’in 1557’de Rusya’ya gönüllü olarak katıldığı yönündeki Sovyet dönemi anlatısını sorgular. Namitok’a göre mevcut belgeler, açık ve karşılıklı rızaya dayanan tek bir katılım kararını kesin biçimde ortaya koymaz; sonraki siyasi anlatılar ise çok daha karmaşık bir tarihi basitleştirmiştir.

kbd.title: Айтек Намиток — Къэбэрдейр Урысейм «и фӏэфӏкӏэ» зэрыгуэхьар
kbd.description: Caucasian Review, Мюнхен, № 2, 1956. 1956 гъэм итха мы тхыгъэм Айтек Намиток Совет зэманым къагупсысауэ Къэбэрдейр 1557 гъэм Урысейм и фӏэфӏкӏэ гуэхьауэ жаӏэм пэщӏоувэ. Абы и гугъэмкӏэ, тхылъхэм къагъэлъагъуэркъым а гуэхьэныгъэр зэгурыӏуэу, хуиту зэрекӏуэкӏар; иужькӏэ политикэм тхыдэ гугъур тыншу ищӏащ.

ru.title: Айтек Намиток — «Добровольное» присоединение Кабарды (Восточной Черкесии) к России
ru.description: Caucasian Review, Мюнхен, № 2, 1956, с. 17 и далее. В этой статье 1956 года Айтек Намиток оспаривает утверждение советской эпохи о том, что Кабарда добровольно присоединилась к России в 1557 году. По его мнению, имеющиеся источники не подтверждают ясного и обоюдно согласованного акта присоединения, а позднейшие политические трактовки упростили гораздо более сложную историю.

de.title: Aytek Namitok — Der „freiwillige“ Anschluss Kabardas (Ost-Tscherkessiens) an Russland
de.description: Caucasian Review, München, Nr. 2, 1956, S. 17 ff. In diesem Artikel aus dem Jahr 1956 widerspricht Aytek Namitok der sowjetischen Behauptung, Kabarda habe sich 1557 freiwillig Russland angeschlossen. Seiner Ansicht nach belegen die Quellen keinen klaren, einvernehmlichen Anschlussakt; spätere politische Darstellungen hätten eine weit komplexere Geschichte vereinfacht.

ar.title: آيتك ناميتوك — الانضمام «الطوعي» لقبردا (شركيسيا الشرقية) إلى روسيا
ar.description: مجلة Caucasian Review، ميونخ، العدد 2، 1956، ص 17 وما بعدها. يفنّد آيتك ناميتوك في مقاله هذا المنشور عام 1956 الادعاء السوفييتي بأن قبردا انضمت طوعًا إلى روسيا عام 1557. ويرى أن الوثائق المتوفرة لا تثبت فعلَ انضمامٍ واضحًا قائمًا على رضا الطرفين، وأن الروايات السياسية اللاحقة بسّطت تاريخًا أكثر تعقيدًا بكثير.

ady.title: Айтэкъо Нэмытӏыкъу — Къэбэртаир Урысыем «шӀоигъоныгъэкӀэ» зэрэхэхьагъэр
ady.description: Caucasian Review, Мюнхен, № 2, 1956. 1956 илъэсым тхыгъэ мыщ Айтэкъо Нэмытӏыкъу Совет лъэхъаным къаӀуагъэу Къэбэртаир 1557 илъэсым Урысыем ежь ышӀоигъоу хэхьагъэу зэраӀорэм пэуцужьы. Авторым зэрилъытэрэмкӀэ, тхылъхэм а шӀоигъоныгъэр къаушыхьатырэп, ыужыкӀэ политикэм итарихъ шъыпкъэр къызэрыкӀо ышӀыгъ.

title: The Circassian Genocide
author: Walter Richmond
description: Rutgers University Press monograph on the Russo-Circassian War, the genocidal campaigns of 1821–22 and 1863–64, and five generations of diaspora up to the Sochi Olympics. Read via Project MUSE with library access, or purchase.

tr.title: Çerkes Soykırımı
tr.author: Walter Richmond · Çeviri: Erdoğan Boz · Koyu Siyah Kitap · ISBN 978-605-81855-1-7 · 272 s.
tr.description: Rutgers University Press'in 2013'te yayımladığı The Circassian Genocide'ın Türkçe çevirisi. Rus–Çerkes Savaşı'nı, 1821–22 ve 1863–64'teki soykırım harekâtlarını, daha önce kullanılmamış arşiv belgelerine dayanarak anlatıyor; sürgün edilen Çerkeslerin diasporadaki beş kuşaklık var olma mücadelesini ve 2014 Soçi Kış Olimpiyatları etrafındaki tartışmaları ele alıyor. Yayınevinden satın alınabilir.

title: The Circassians: A Forgotten Genocide?
author: Stephen D. Shenfield
description: Chapter 7 of The Massacre in History, edited by Mark Levene and Penny Roberts (Berghahn Books, War and Genocide vol. 1). Examines the massacres and deportations of the 1860s and asks whether they amount to genocide. Available from the publisher.

title: Imperial Refuge: Resettlement of Muslims from Russia in the Ottoman Empire, 1860–1914
author: Vladimir Hamed-Troyansky · Stanford University
description: How the Ottoman state resettled about a million North Caucasian refugees in the Balkans, Anatolia and the Levant, based on archives in Turkey, Jordan, Bulgaria, Russia, Georgia and the UK. Free to download (CC BY-NC-ND) from the Stanford Digital Repository.

title: The Circassian Revival: A Quest for Recognition
author: Lars Funch Hansen · University of Copenhagen
description: Transnational Circassian mobilisation and memorialisation, and the campaign to have the 1864 exile recognised as genocide. The thesis is unpublished: request a copy through the University of Copenhagen library or from the author.

title: Civil War, Violence and Nationality from Empire to Nation State: The Circassians in Turkey (1918–1938)
author: Caner Yelbaşı · SOAS University of London
description: The Circassian diaspora in Anatolia from the last Ottoman years to the early Turkish Republic. Free to download (CC BY-NC-ND) from the SOAS research repository.

title: The First 'Circassian Exodus' to the Ottoman Empire (1858–1867), and the Ottoman Response
author: Sarah A. S. Isla Rosser-Owen · SOAS University of London
description: The arrival of Circassian refugees in Ottoman Black Sea ports and the Ottoman response, based on the reports of British consuls, journalists and other eyewitnesses.

title: Ukraine's and Georgia's Recognition of the Circassian Genocide: Strategic Engagement with North Caucasian Causes
author: Matthew Kelbaugh · Journal of Caucasian Studies 10 (16): 79–116
description: How Georgia (2011) and Ukraine have recognised the Circassian genocide, and what these recognitions mean for the politics of memory and for stateless peoples resisting Russian rule.

title: Position and Diplomatic Demarches of Great Britain in Connection with the Exodus of the Circassians to the Ottoman Empire in 1864
author: Georgy V. Chochiev · Caucasology no. 4: 73–89 · DOI 10.31143/2542-212X-2025-4-73-89
description: Based on British diplomatic correspondence: how the Foreign Office handled the mass exodus of 1863–64, and why London declined to act. Article in Russian with an English abstract.

title: Immigration and Settlement of Circassians in the Ottoman Empire on British Documents, 1857–1864
author: Musa Şaşmaz · OTAM 9: 331–366
description: A detailed reconstruction from Foreign Office files (FO 97/424, FO 881) of the expulsion, the refugee camps at Trabzon and Samsun, mortality at sea and the settlement of survivors across the Ottoman Empire.

title: Immigration and Settlement of Abkhazians in the Ottoman Empire on British Documents, 1864–67
author: Musa Şaşmaz
description: The sequel to the Circassian exodus: the removal of the Prince of Abkhazia, the forced emigration of 1867 and the separation of families, as recorded by British consuls.

title: The Struggle over the Circassian Genocide: Between Historical Recognition and Current Practicalities
author: Michael Geheran & Chen Bram · Clark University, CHGS Conference Proceedings
description: Paper from Clark University's Strassler Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies on the politics of recognising the Circassian genocide.

title: The Russian Final Subjugation of Northwestern Caucasus: Colonial Atrocities and European Responsibilities
author: Irma Kreiten · University of Southampton
description: Paper presented at the Circassian Day in the European Parliament, Brussels, on Russian colonial policy and ethnic cleansing in the Northwest Caucasus and Europe's share of responsibility.

title: Черкесия: историко-этнографические статьи
author: Л. Я. Люлье · переиздание: «Возрождение», 1990
description: Сборник четырёх статей Леонтия Люлье, впервые опубликованных в «Записках Кавказского отдела Русского географического общества» (кн. IV, 1857; кн. V, 1862; кн. VII, 1866): общий обзор земель черкесов, абхазов и соседних горских народов; о натухайцах, шапсугах и абадзехах; верования, религиозные обряды и предрассудки черкесов; учреждения и народные обычаи шапсугов и натухайцев. Свидетельство очевидца последних лет независимости Черкесии.

tr.title: Çerkesya: Tarihi–Etnografik Makaleler (1857–1862–1866)
tr.author: Leonti Lyulye · Çeviri: Murat Topçu · ISBN 9786259568379 · 115 s.
tr.description: Fransız kökenli etnograf ve dilbilimci Leonti Lyulye'nin 1857, 1862 ve 1866'da Rus Coğrafya Kurumu Kafkasya Şubesi'nin yayın organında çıkan makalelerinin Rusçadan çevirisi. Çerkeslerin, Abhazların ve komşu dağlı halkların yerleşim alanlarını, toplumsal kurumlarını, inançlarını, dini törenlerini ve geleneklerini, Çerkes bağımsızlık mücadelesinin son yıllarından bir tanık olarak anlatıyor. Yayınevinden satın alınabilir.

title: Последний год войны Черкесии за независимость. 1863–1864 гг.
author: А. Фонвилль · Из записок участника-иностранца · ред. Х. Г. Кармоков · Нальчик: журнал «Адыги», 1991
description: Записки француза, находившегося среди черкесов на черноморском побережье в последний год их борьбы за независимость, 1863–1864. Свидетельство очевидца о последних сражениях западных черкесов против Российской империи и о трагедии народа накануне изгнания.

tr.title: Çerkesya Bağımsızlık Savaşının Son Yılı (1863–1864)
tr.author: Arthur de Fonvielle · Çeviri: Murat Topçu · ISBN 9786259568324 · 104 s.
tr.description: 1863–1864'te Karadeniz kıyısında direnen Çerkeslerin arasında bulunan Fransız yazar Arthur de Fonvielle'in tanıklığı. Batı Çerkeslerinin Rus İmparatorluğu'na karşı bağımsızlık mücadelesinin son dönemini, yok oluşla karşı karşıya kalan bir halkın onurunu koruma çabasıyla birlikte anlatıyor. Yayınevinden satın alınabilir.
